rationale: Two changes to the exploration, both motivated by its own results. First, the leader-completeness monitor was wrong: it evaluated completeness continuously, so a stale partitioned leader that had not yet seen a higher term was reported as lacking a committed entry (the earlier local run produced four false positives of the form 'leader 1 at term 3 lacks index 4 term 10'). Completeness is owed only by a newly elected leader for entries committed before its election, so the monitor now fires only on a leadership transition. Second, membership changes are now injected, which is the axis of interest for this snapshot: leaders randomly propose ConfChangeV2 operations adding or removing a learner id and removing or re-adding voter 3, applied through the captured conf-change interface with any apply panic recorded as an event rather than crashing the run. Fresh execution is requested for the changed harness.

experiment.revision_reason: Harness and monitor change: (1) the leader-completeness monitor now evaluates only when a state machine transitions into StateLeader, because the previous predicate also flagged stale partitioned leaders that had not seen the higher term, which is not a completeness violation and produced four false positives in a local run; (2) the exploration now injects membership changes, with a leader randomly proposing a ConfChangeV2 that adds or removes a learner id (10 or 11) or removes/re-adds voter 3, applied through the captured conf-change interface inside a recover that records any apply panic as a conf_change_apply_panic event; (3) counters for attempted and accepted conf changes are reported in the summary. Seeds, step count, loss model and the other monitors are unchanged.

scope.description: Exploration with no fixed requirement: three real raft state machines (ids 1,2,3, ElectionTick 10, HeartbeatTick 1, in-memory storage whose ConfState is {1,2,3}) driven for 300 steps per seed with random connectivity masks that change the reachable peers, per-message drop decisions, random ticks, random member proposals, random campaigns, random leader transfer requests and random membership-change proposals (add or remove a learner id, remove or re-add voter 3). Committed entries are applied through the captured log interface, conf changes are applied through the captured conf-change interface with apply panics recorded as events, and safety monitors run after every step: one leader per term, applied entries immutable per node and index, identical entry for the same index across nodes, committed index monotonic per node, and completeness of previously applied entries evaluated at each leadership transition.
assumptions: Messages are delivered in random batches of up to three per step and may be dropped, modelling lossy, reordering-prone transport without permanent partitions.
Confinement masks change independently per node, so asymmetric partitions occur.
Entries are persisted to the in-memory storage through the captured helpers before messages are delivered.

Membership changes are proposed only by a node that reports itself leader and has a progress entry for itself; a changed configuration may still be applied on another node from a stale base, which is exactly one of the interleavings under exploration.
excluded: Snapshot transfer, restart recovery and crash-stop faults
Any claim of absence of defects beyond the explored seeds and 300 steps each
Liveness claims: the monitors are safety-style only

experiment.prefix: For each seed in {11, 23}: create three raft state machines with in-memory storage whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3}. Loop 300 steps; each step may change the per-node reachability masks, tick some state machines, step a random proposal on a member, step a random campaign, step a random leader transfer request, and step a membership change proposed by whichever selected node reports itself leader (add or remove a learner id, or remove/re-add voter 3). Then collect outbound messages (dropping those between unreachable peers or per a random drop decision), shuffle and deliver at most three messages, and finally persist and apply committed entries, applying conf changes as they appear while recording any apply panic as an event, and run the safety monitors (completeness only at leadership transitions), emitting a violation event per failure and one summary per seed.
